D1.name: Binary phylogenetic tree
D1.clean_text: A binary phylogenetic tree, [MATH]T=(V,E,φ)[/MATH] on a finite set of taxa [MATH]X[/MATH], is a triple consisting of a finite set of vertices, V , a set [MATH]E[/MATH] of edges between vertices, and a "labeling" map [MATH]φ : X → L[/MATH], where [MATH]L ⊂ V[/MATH] contains all vertices of degree one or leaves, such that the graph [MATH](V,E)[/MATH] is an unrooted binary tree and the map [MATH]φ[/MATH] induces a bijection between [MATH]X[/MATH] and the set [MATH]L[/MATH] of leaves of [MATH]T[/MATH].

D2.name: Phylogenetic tree isomorphism
D2.clean_text: Phylogenetic trees, [MATH]T_1=(V_1, E_1, φ_1)[/MATH] and [MATH]T_2=(V_2, E_2, φ_2)[/MATH] on a taxon set [MATH]X[/MATH], are isomorphic if there exists a bijective map [MATH]f : V_1 → V_2[/MATH], called an isomorphism, such that if [MATH]{u,v} ∈ E_1[/MATH] then [MATH]{f(u), f(v)} ∈ E_2[/MATH] and for every [MATH]x ∈ X[/MATH] we have [MATH]φ_2(x)=f(φ_1(x))[/MATH].

D3.name: Distinguished edge
D3.clean_text: Let [MATH]T = (V,E,φ)[/MATH] be a binary phylogenetic tree and let [MATH]ab|cd ∈ Q_T[/MATH]. An interior edge [MATH]e[/MATH] of [MATH]T[/MATH] is distinguished by [MATH]ab|cd[/MATH] if [MATH]e[/MATH] is the only edge that separates [MATH]a[/MATH] and [MATH]b[/MATH] from [MATH]c[/MATH] and [MATH]d[/MATH].

D4.name: Definitive system of quartet trees
D4.clean_text: A system of quartet trees, [MATH]Q[/MATH], is definitive, if up to isomorphism, there exists a unique binary phylogenetic tree [MATH]T[/MATH] for which [MATH]Q ⊆ Q_T[/MATH].

D5.label: order
D5.name: Associated graph for quartet trees
D5.clean_text: For a compatible system of [MATH]n-3[/MATH] quartet trees [MATH]Q[/MATH] on a taxon set [MATH]X[/MATH], define the associated graph [MATH]G_T(Q)[/MATH] with vertex set [MATH]V[/MATH] and edge set [MATH]E[/MATH] as follows: The vertex set [MATH]V[/MATH] is the set of all quartet trees [MATH]q ∈ Q[/MATH] which distinguish a unique edge in [MATH]T[/MATH]. Vertex pairs [MATH]{q_i,q_j}[/MATH] are connected by an edge [MATH]e ∈ E[/MATH] if the edge [MATH]e_i[/MATH] that [MATH]q_i[/MATH] distinguishes is adjacent to the edge [MATH]e_j[/MATH] that [MATH]q_j[/MATH] distinguishes and [MATH]|supp({q_i,q_j})|=5[/MATH].

D6.name: Linked quartet trees and linked system
D6.clean_text: Two quartet trees are linked if their vertices are connected in [MATH]G_T(Q)[/MATH]. The system of quartet trees [MATH]Q[/MATH], is a linked system if [MATH]G_T(Q)[/MATH] is connected.

D7.name: Phylogenetically decisive
D7.clean_text: We say that [MATH]S[/MATH] is phylogenetically decisive if it satisfies the following property: If [MATH]T[/MATH] and [MATH]T'[/MATH] are binary phylogenetic trees, with [MATH]T|Y=T'|Y[/MATH] for all [MATH]Y ∈ S[/MATH], then [MATH]T=T'[/MATH].

D8.name: Caterpillar tree
D8.raw_latex:
\begin{defn} (\cite{semple}) A \emph{caterpillar} on $n$ leaves is a binary phylogenetic tree for which there exists an induced subtree on a sequence of distinct interior vertices $v_1,v_2,...,v_k$ such that, for all $i \in \{1,2,...,k-1\}$, $v_i$ and $v_{i+1}$ are adjacent.
\end{defn}
D8.clean_text: A caterpillar on [MATH]n[/MATH] leaves is a binary phylogenetic tree for which there exists an induced subtree on a sequence of distinct interior vertices [MATH]v_1,v_2,...,v_k[/MATH] such that, for all [MATH]i ∈ {1,2,...,k-1}[/MATH], [MATH]v_i[/MATH] and [MATH]v_{i+1}[/MATH] are adjacent.

D9.name: Quartet tree substitution
D9.raw_latex:
\begin{defn} Let $q=ij|kh$ be a quartet tree that distinguishes an edge $e$ and let $i \in A_i$, $j \in A_j$, $k \in A_k$, and $h \in A_h$, where $A_i$, $A_j$, $A_k$, and $A_h$ are partitions of $X$ induced by $e$. For $x\in X - supp(q)$  define the \emph{quartet tree substitution} $q(x)$ to be the unique quartet tree in which the taxon $x \in A_n$ replaces the taxon in $q$ that is in $supp(q) \cap A_n$.
\end{defn}

For [MATH]x∈ X - supp(q)[/MATH] define the quartet tree substitution [MATH]q(x)[/MATH] to be the unique quartet tree in which the taxon [MATH]x ∈ A_n[/MATH] replaces the taxon in [MATH]q[/MATH] that is in [MATH]supp(q) ∩ A_n[/MATH].

D10.name: Vine of quartet tree
D10.clean_text: Let the quartet tree [MATH]q[/MATH] distinguish an edge [MATH]e[/MATH] of a tree. Define the vine of q by [MATH]v(q)={q} ∪ ⋃_{x∈ X-supp(q)}q(x)[/MATH]. We refer to [MATH]q[/MATH] as the seed of the vine.

D11.name: Linked vines
D11.clean_text: Two vines [MATH]v(q_i)[/MATH] and [MATH]v(q_j)[/MATH] are linked if for each [MATH]q_i ∈ v(q_i)[/MATH] there exists a unique [MATH]q_j ∈ v(q_j)[/MATH] such that [MATH]q_i[/MATH] and [MATH]q_j[/MATH] are linked.

D12.name: Meshed system
D12.clean_text: A meshed system on a tree [MATH]T[/MATH] with taxon set [MATH]X[/MATH] is an [MATH](n-3)[/MATH] by [MATH](n-3)[/MATH] array of quartet trees, where each row is a linked system and each column is a vine.
